title: Towards a Measure Theory of Semantic Information
content: The classic account of the quantification of semantic information is that of Bar Hillel and Carnap. However, their approach assigns the maximum informativeness to a contradiction. This situation is what Floridi refers to as the Bar Hillel-Carnap paradox, and he developed a novel theory designed to remove this paradox. Unfortunately his approach does not succeed in that aim. In this paper I critique Floridi’s theory of strongly semantic information on its own terms and show where it succeeds and fails. I then present a novel approach based on methods from communication theory and quantum probability that meets all the requirements stipulated by Floridi and removes the paradox.
